CBSA.CICSBSA.ABNDFILE.recovery_why: etc/install/base/installjcl/BANK.csd: DEFINE FILE(ABNDFILE) ... RECOVERY(NONE) -- the abend log a backout must not undo

scenarios.name: first-entry
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN 0: WS-COMM-AREA initialised, the map sent ERASE with the cursor on ACCNO; RETURN TRANSID('ODAC') LENGTH(102)

scenarios.name: pa1
scenarios.why: PA1: CONTINUE, nothing sent; RETURN TRANSID with the COMMAREA

scenarios.name: pf3
scenarios.why: PF3: RETURN TRANSID('OMEN') IMMEDIATE: back to the main menu

scenarios.name: clear
scenarios.why: CLEAR: SEND CONTROL ERASE FREEKB, RETURN

scenarios.name: mapfail
scenarios.why: ENTER with no field modified: RM010 -- ABNDPROC LINKed (an ABNDFILE record) and ABEND HBNK

scenarios.name: other-key
scenarios.why: PF7: WHEN OTHER -- 'Invalid key pressed.', SEND MAP DATAONLY ALARM (PF5 is this screen's delete key)

notes: BNK1DAC on generated Db2 rows (#4507): the display / delete screen of cbsa-bnk1dac, its LINKed INQACC and DELACC and the tables ACCOUNT and PROCTRAN compared after every task, with ACCOUNT rows generated from the DDL (30 rows, boundary values, NULLs) and the typed / carried account numbers drawn from them (the screen's ACCNO2 always one a row holds: a number that is not one makes the Java NUMVAL throw where GnuCOBOL's reads 0, see the PR; ACCNO and the carried COMMAREA number miss 15% of the time). Stated scenarios keep the non-ENTER / non-PF5 keys and MAPFAIL; the inquiries and deletes are generated. Derived from the CICS Bank Sample Application (CBSA), EPL-2.0: LICENSE is the corpus's own.
